title: Cortex MemoryPromoteRequest (DRAFT v0)
description: Canonical wire shape for POST /promote on mnemos. Mirrors the historical main.py:PromoteRequest BaseModel but is the SINGLE source of truth per ADR-0014; main.py imports and re-types it. The keystone is `additionalProperties:false` — without it a producer could inject rogue fields (e.g. undeclared provenance metadata, hidden attestor overrides) that consumers would silently pick up. `memory_id` and `to_container` are the only required fields; `attestor` is server-required (promotion is a reviewed ritual, never automatic) but optional on the wire so the keystone can emit a clean 'attestor required' message before the handler's own check. The `to_container` MUST be a protected-root container — ordinary containers belong on /store. Status: DRAFT; bump $id on breaking changes. Note: this is the WRITE shape for the review/attest ritual; the promoted memory's full row carries additional server-stamped fields (promoted_memory_id, attestation_id, from_container, promoted_at) that are NEVER accepted on input.

memory_id.description: The memory id to promote. Must be a real, non-tombstoned memory row. Server-side 404s on missing.

to_container.description: Target protected-root container. Server normalizes via normalize_container_tag() and asserts is_protected_root() — non-root targets 400 with the canonical 'use /store for ordinary containers' guidance. Examples: 'cortex', 'thislive', 'mnemos'.

attestor.description: WHO is attesting this promotion is a reviewed ritual (human | system:cron-name | mcp-bridge:user). Required at the handler level (400 if absent) but optional on the wire so the keystone's first pass is shape-only and the handler's second pass enforces the business rule.

reason.description: Free-form WHY this memory is being promoted. Recorded in the audit log alongside the attestation_id. Optional but encouraged.
